name: Duskline Banded Collar Shirt
description:
A clean, relaxed banded-collar shirt cut from a medium-weight cotton-modal blend in a deep indigo that fades slightly at the seams — intentional, not wear. The collar sits close without choking, the placket runs four buttons down, and the hem is cut slightly longer in the back for tucking or leaving out. Sleeves can be rolled and stayed with a small interior button tab. It breathes well, drapes well, and looks equally at home in a Tier 3 apartment kitchen or a mid-range restaurant.

Favored by people who want to look put-together without looking like they're trying. The Duskline shirt has been in continuous production by Veramar Goods for over a decade with minimal changes — the kind of product that stays in the catalog because it simply works. You see it on schoolteachers, freelance architects, and the occasional off-duty transit cop.
what_it_says: I have taste and I don't need to prove it.
story_hooks: A character finds one still in its original packaging inside a derelict Tier 3 apartment — the previous tenant left in a hurry and never came back.
Veramar Goods has been quietly bought out by a corponation; the next production run will carry a corporate wellness logo on the hem. The old stock is quietly becoming collectible.
Someone wearing this shirt is found dead in a Tier 1 access corridor — the shirt is clean, pristine, and completely out of place.

physical_description.visual_profile: A understated, classically proportioned banded-collar shirt with a relaxed yet refined silhouette. The deep indigo creates a sophisticated foundation that reads neither corporate nor street—occupies the middle ground of Tier 3 respectability. The slightly longer back hem and rollable sleeves suggest versatility without affectation.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but not loose; tailored enough to suggest intentionality without compression. Sleeves taper gently to the wrist. Torso has room for layering or natural movement. Back hem extends 2-3 inches longer than front, enabling multiple wear styles.
physical_description.primary_material: Cotton-modal blend, medium weight—breathable and durable without technical sheen or augmentation integration
physical_description.texture: Smooth hand with subtle matte finish. The fabric has a lived-in drape despite being new. Seams show intentional subtle fading, creating depth without distressing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep indigo base (#1a3a52 equivalent) with deliberately faded striations along seams and sleeve edges. No patterns—solid colorway allows adaptability across contexts.
physical_description.closures: Four-button placket in matte gunmetal; banded collar sits without fastener, held by internal structure
distinctive_features: Interior button tab on sleeves for rolling and securing
Banded collar—no points, sits flush and comfortable against neck
Intentional seam fading creates subtle visual interest without wear-degradation
Longer back hem—functional for tucking or drape
Veramar Goods woven label at inside neck, understated branding
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 aspirational—signals stability and taste without luxury pretension. Affordable enough for working class, quality enough to command respect.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by knowledge workers, transit employees, educators, and creatives who prioritize functionality and quiet competence. The shirt says 'I have my life together' without announcing it. Anti-hype, anti-chrome, pro-substance.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new, but within weeks develops a broken-in softness. Seams remain sharp; fabric develops subtle wear patterns at cuffs and collar. Washing deepens the indigo slightly. Remains wearable for years.
